findings: The plate accurately identifies Bay-breasted Warbler as Setophaga castanea in family Parulidae.

The primary illustration credibly depicts a nonbreeding female/immature-type bird: low-contrast olive head and back, pale unstreaked underparts, buff-olive flanks, dark wings with two bold white wingbars, and dark eye, legs, and feet.

The primary specimen has one head, one bill, a complete and convincing wing pair with the far wing naturally occluded, two attached legs with intact feet, and one coherent tail. The detached wing and head-and-bill studies are clearly supplementary.
Both depicted bills are now short, slender, straight, sharply tapered, and co-terminal; neither dark upper mandible visibly overhangs the pale lower mandible.
The folded wings, compact square-to-slightly-notched tail, dark legs, perching feet, eye placement, and overall body proportions are anatomically credible and consistent with the attached references.
The wing study independently shows the species’ dark flight feathers and two bold white wingbars without appearing attached to the primary specimen.
Every visible taxonomy, measurement, habitat, behavior, field-mark, and palette line matches the proposed profile, including the corrected palette wording “dark charcoal gray.”

The Cornell measurement set directly supports 5.5 in (14 cm) length, 0.3–0.6 oz (10–17 g) weight, and 7.9–8.7 in (20–22 cm) wingspan for both sexes. Audubon publishes a compatible but broader set, which does not create a profile conflict.
The ruler runs from 0 at the bottom to 5.5 in (14 cm) at the top, agrees with the stated length, and is explicitly labeled “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE.”
The habitat and behavior prose is consistent with the independently verified Cornell and Audubon accounts.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears.
